title: Wax candle flame morphology and dried kombucha SCOBY as candidate wick

provenance.origin: Owner discussion on candle-flame shape, comparison to sprite/game-engine rendering, and request to examine a dried kombucha pellicle wick.

research_questions: Where, physically, is a candle flame's visible shape formed?
Why does it resemble a game-engine sprite while not being a rendered two-dimensional surface?
Can dried SCOBY-derived bacterial-cellulose pellicle wick molten candle wax sufficiently for stable burning?

candle_flame.scope: Ordinary wax candle in Earth-normal gravity, quiescent air.
process_sequence: Radiant and conducted heat melts wax near wick.
Liquid wax travels through capillaries in the wick.
Hot wax vaporizes and may thermally decompose into smaller fuel molecules.
Fuel vapor and air oxygen mix, producing a diffusion flame in a region around the wick.
Exothermic reactions heat surrounding gases and support vaporization; stable combustion requires sustained fuel and oxygen supply.
Lower-density hot gases rise by buoyant convection, stretching the flame vertically.
Fuel oxidation, entrainment, and diffusion change the reaction zone along its upward path.

why_a_shape_exists.spatial_medium: The ambient gas; flame is a non-solid region of reactions, temperature and radiation, not a separate object with a physical skin.
principal_drivers: oxygen transport by diffusion and convection
why_a_shape_exists.why_teardrop: Rising hot gases deform the reaction/soot fields into a narrow rising plume while fuel and oxygen are consumed and mixed.
why_a_shape_exists.why_persistent: A near-steady flow-through structure maintains an approximately recognizable shape while the individual molecules are continually replaced.
why_a_shape_exists.why_flickering: Time-dependent buoyant flow, environmental air currents, heat release and instabilities modulate luminous regions.
why_a_shape_exists.caveat: The visible yellow contour is not exactly the boundary of the hottest gas or chemical reaction zone.

optical_appearance.visible_yellow: Primarily incandescent soot particles formed in fuel-rich zones, with local differences in soot density and temperature.
optical_appearance.blue_regions: Can involve molecular chemiluminescence and lower soot abundance; blue color is not a simple thermometer.
optical_appearance.transparent_regions: Different gas regions absorb and emit differently; optical integration occurs along a viewing ray.
optical_appearance.visual_brightness: Determined by line-of-sight emission and absorption, not by a single rigid glowing shell.
optical_appearance.potential_misconception: The brightest yellow region should not automatically be labeled the hottest region.

game_approximations: additive blending as a visual effect
relation_to_sprites.crucial_difference: Physical combustion is a 3D continuous chemical/fluid process; sprites are a rendering approximation, not evidence that reality runs on discrete frames.
relation_to_sprites.falsification_or_prediction: Changing gravity, air currents and wick geometry should alter real flame morphology even with no change in visual observer; rendering parameters alone do not define the physical flame.

microgravity_control.grounded_observation: Microgravity candles can show dim blue roughly spherical/hemispherical flames due to the absence of terrestrial buoyancy-driven convection.
microgravity_control.relevance: Demonstrates that gravity-dependent gas flow strongly affects ordinary candle-flame shape.

scoby_material.definition: Dried kombucha pellicle: cellulose-rich network, possibly also containing microbes, residual proteins, organic acids, sugars, and fermentation residues; it is not automatically equivalent to purified bacterial cellulose.
scoby_material.mechanism_under_test: Whether its wetted microstructure and manufactured geometry create continuous capillary channels for molten wax, while retaining useful charring/structural behavior.
reasons_to_test: Cellulose can form a fibrous porous network.
Natural-fiber candle wicks can carry molten wax by capillarity.
SCOBY-derived cellulose is manufacturable as films and rolls.
main_uncertainties: Drying can collapse pores and make membranes compact/brittle.
Water absorption is NOT evidence of molten-wax uptake or wetting.
Wax viscosity, surface tension, contact angle and pore connectivity for the actual specimen are unknown.
Pellicle residue, variability and microbiological impurities may affect combustion emissions.
Self-consumption/char formation may be too rapid or may block supply; no combustion observations exist for this specimen.

evidence_summary.dried_microstructure: Literature reports drying-method-dependent collapses of bacterial-cellulose porous structures and reductions in dry handling performance.
evidence_summary.thermal_degradation: Published kombucha cellulose studies report onset of thermal degradation roughly 250–330 °C depending on preparation; degradation onset is NOT the flash/ignition temperature of a finished wick.
evidence_summary.aqueous_absorption: Hydrophilicity and water sorption have been measured, but are insufficient to conclude wax transport.
evidence_summary.state_of_prior_art: No retrieved source here establishes that a raw dried SCOBY pellicle can serve as a stable candle wick.

hypotheses.claim: Certain SCOBY fiber geometries may sustain wax transport and a normal diffusion flame.
hypotheses.test: Compare steady capillary supply and flame lifetime against cotton wick at matched wax and controlled geometry.

hypotheses.claim: A dense air-dried sheet may be a weak wick because pore collapse reduces permeability.
hypotheses.test: Compare pore structure and matched wax uptake between dense and more open-prepared sheets.

hypotheses.claim: Geometry adjustment may improve transport but produce different char, smoke or stability.
hypotheses.test: Blind randomized comparison of prepared sheet/rolled strand and controls; inspect soot and char.

desktop_experiment.model: Simplified Darcy supply proxy Q ∝ k*A*DeltaP/(mu*L). Relative to a matched cotton reference: Q_index=(k_scoby/k_cotton)*(DeltaP_scoby/DeltaP_cotton), assuming identical wax, wick cross-section, length, no gravitational head, and constant saturated effective permeability.

result_summary.interpretation: The reduced model admits both lower and higher theoretical supply under different unmeasured properties; it cannot determine which regime the real SCOBY sample occupies.

assumptions: Relative permeability values were arbitrarily selected for sensitivity analysis, not obtained from SCOBY samples.
Relative capillary pressure values were arbitrarily selected; no wax contact-angle measurements exist.
No evaporation feedback, thermal degradation, transient wicking, gravitational head, shrinking wet section or chemistry is represented.
Normalized index is not a predicted flame height or burning time.

preregistered_physical_validation_plan.study_type: Comparative materials-and-flame experiment under fire laboratory supervision

groups.material: Dried washed unpurified kombucha pellicle, strip
Dried purified bacterial cellulose sheet, strip
Dried rolled or woven SCOBY pellicle

controlled_conditions: Same wax batch and vessel type
Document specimen dry mass, dimensions and drying treatment
Equivalent immersed and exposed wick geometry where achievable; record any deviations
Controlled ambient airflow and air temperature
Consistent video viewpoint, exposure settings and mass measurement
Randomized trial order and blank observer forms
stage_A_non_combustion: Verify basic dryness, intact geometry and sample classification; do not infer purification from appearance.
Measure thickness, mass, porosity proxy, and bending/fragility.
Screen fluid uptake with safe non-combustible test fluids only as a screening proxy and explicitly separate these from molten-wax compatibility.
Establish a specialist-supervised non-flame protocol for actual molten-wax wetting/permeability if the candidate passes preliminary screens.
stage_B_combustion_if_authorized: Use an approved controlled combustion bench/enclosure with trained personnel and appropriate extinguishing means; no unattended or indoor hobby testing.
Collect matched comparison measurements of wick fed flame, self-extinguishing, mass loss, char formation and emissions.
Stop immediately for unexpected spreading flame, abnormal smoke, uncontrolled melted-wax behavior or loss of containment.
analysis_plan: Preserve all replicates including extinguished runs and negative results.
Report central tendencies and variability, not only best-performing candidate.
Compare S1/S2/S3 independently to C0 and account for unmatched geometry as a confounder.
Do not claim practical wick viability until repeated stable burns and acceptable emissions are established.
Use a reserved raw-data path and compute hashes for videos/measurements after real trials.
preregistered_physical_validation_plan.go_no_go: No physical launch without laboratory safety setup, material characterization and an operator able to extinguish unforeseen flames.

safety_and_boundaries: This JSON is an analysis and pre-registration, not permission to leave a prototype candle burning unattended.
SCOBY is not automatically clean, safe, low-soot or low-emission merely because it is a biomaterial.
Do not burn specimens treated with unknown additives, solvents, glues or coatings.
Avoid breathing smoke from uncharacterized samples.
A desktop sensitivity sweep is not a fire test, an experimental success, or a proof of functional wick equivalence.

next_gate.acceptance_requirement: Material-identified, matched-control capillary/wax and safely supervised combustion measurements with full data, video and negative results.

specific_historical_arm.archival_note: A proposed characterization branch was found, not an executed oil sorption or fire experiment.
safeguards: Do not interpret porous appearance as proof of engineered aerogel or hydrophobicity.
No household microwave recipes for dried biopolymer treatment or unknown residues.
No new functional claims without sample identity, process history, density, porosity, surface chemistry, oil/water uptake, emissions and contaminants.

background_oil_sorbent_program.literature_high_capacity_belongs_to: Engineered bacterial-cellulose aerogels in third-party literature, not raw or microwaved SCOBY-D0.

cross_hypothesis.distinction: Oil spill remediation favors high uptake and retention plus preferential oil-over-water wettability. A candle wick must provide sustained directed molten wax transport through a thermally exposed wick with an appropriate capillary network and stable charring behavior. The optimum pore geometry/surface chemistry may differ, or be in tension, between the two applications.
identified_confounds: Porosity can improve initial uptake without supplying directional continuous liquid flow.
Hydrophobic treatment may increase oil-water selectivity, but may change molten wax wetting and emissions.
Microwave-generated char, chemical heterogeneity and damaged networks may be poor wick material even when visually porous.
Residual contaminated sorbent must never be burned as a wick.
cross_hypothesis.followup_candidate: Only consider controlled, characterized, uncontaminated D5 specimens for a separate materials review; do not elevate D5 to physical candle tests on the basis of prior oil-sorbent hypotheses alone.

recovered_prior_project.provenance_limit: Current search covered exact project records, research lineage and designated oil sorption files; this is not a complete forensic scan of all offline NAS or legacy raw laboratory media.
